content:
For Fiber to the Home (FTTH), the most common protocol used for internet access is Passive Optical Network (PON) technology. Specifically, there are several variants of PON protocols:

1. GPON (Gigabit Passive Optical Network)
- Most widely deployed
- Offers downstream speeds up to 2.5 Gbps
- Upstream speeds up to 1.25 Gbps
- Used by many telecommunications providers

2. XG-PON (10-Gigabit PON)
- Higher bandwidth
- Downstream speeds up to 10 Gbps
- Upstream speeds up to 2.5 Gbps

3. NG-PON2 (Next-Generation Passive Optical Network 2)
- Most advanced PON technology
- Can support multiple wavelengths
- Potential downstream speeds up to 40 Gbps

4. EPON (Ethernet Passive Optical Network)
- Commonly used in some regions, especially Asia
- Uses Ethernet technology
- Typically offers symmetrical speeds

These protocols use fiber optic cables to provide high-speed internet access directly to homes using a point-to-multipoint architecture.
